questions.title: Does a €300 service-desk voucher 'in lieu of compensation' offset 14C's €600?
questions.found: 14C (NS31) holds a €300 service-desk voucher 'in lieu of compensation' with no signed acceptance on file. CRM records the voucher as accepted; there is no signature hash.
questions.why_flagged: Art. 7(3) needs signed acceptance for an offset, and the sources disagree. No precedent for unsigned in-lieu vouchers.
questions.recommends: No signed acceptance, no offset: pay cash; the voucher stays as goodwill.
questions.recommended_option: Pay €600 cash; the voucher stays as goodwill
options: Pay €600 cash; the voucher stays as goodwill
Offset the voucher: pay the balance in cash
Ask the passenger to sign the acceptance first

questions.title: Is the return sector of a storm-cancelled rotation extraordinary when both ends were calm?
questions.found: Knock-on: NS112 was cancelled for weather, so EI-NSJ never reached LIS; LIS calm at STD, DUB calm at STA. Legal question (C-74/19). Knock-on: NS114 was cancelled for weather, so EI-NSK never reached FCO; FCO calm at STD, DUB calm at STA. Legal question (C-74/19). Knock-on: NS116 was cancelled for weather, so EI-NSL never reached MUC; MUC calm at STD, DUB calm at STA. Legal question (C-74/19).
questions.why_flagged: No precedent for this pattern; the law needs a ruling (C-74/19: direct causal link and reasonable measures).
questions.recommends: Extraordinary only if no aircraft and crew could operate the return within 3 h of STD and passengers were offered the earliest reroute on any carrier (C-74/19).
questions.recommended_option: Extraordinary if no aircraft within 3 h of STD and the earliest reroute was offered
options: Extraordinary if no aircraft within 3 h of STD and the earliest reroute was offered
Not extraordinary: compensation owed on all of them
